bull_bear.body:
- Vertically integrated value chain across design, branding, sourcing, logistics, pricing, display, promotion and selling for Westside and Zudio, enabling fast concept-to-store conversion
- Over 80% of Westside merchandise and nearly all Zudio merchandise near-shored/sourced from within India, giving supply-chain agility, speed and transparency
- Exclusive in-house brand portfolio (not third-party labels) supporting a more balanced/sustainable return-on-capital-employed profile versus third-party retail models
- Deep customer loyalty engagement: WestStyleClub subscription programme reached 11.85 million active members (up 53% YoY) with over 90% of Westside revenue attributable to loyal WSC members
- Multi-brand portfolio strategy addressing distinct price tiers and customer segments (Westside, Zudio, Samoh, Burnt Toast) rather than reliance on a single brand
- Tata Group affiliation and governance culture (Tata Code of Conduct, Tata Business Excellence Model) supporting brand trust
- Disciplined, differentiated store economics with a rigorous property-selection process and active store optimisation/consolidation programme
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependency on the Inditex Group for the Zara and Massimo Dutti associate businesses — Inditex Trent Retail India Pvt Ltd (Zara) and Massimo Dutti India Pvt Ltd, in which the Company holds 20%, are obliged to source merchandise only from the Inditex Group, with product choice and specifications at Inditex's discretion, and depend on Inditex for permission to use the brands in India. Management states this makes the related commitments more akin to a financial investment than a strategic one, and flags valuation uncertainty given operational control rests with the majority partner.
- Depreciation drag from new-store additions weighing on near-term profitability — Newer stores carry higher depreciation relative to revenue, impacting EBITDA in their early years; profitability normalises only as stores mature, making the mix of new versus mature stores in the portfolio a structural driver of consolidated margin volatility.
- Loss-making group entities in food/grocery and wholesale operations — Booker India Limited (51%-owned, cash-and-carry/Booker Wholesale) reported a loss before exceptional items and tax of Rs 7.25 Crore in FY26 (Rs 29.74 Crore loss in FY25), and Fiora Hypermarket Limited (wholly owned, operates Star, Zudio co-located stores and StarQuik) reported a loss before exceptional items and tax of Rs 8.80 Crore in FY26 (Rs 14.53 Crore in FY25) — continued cash drag from these businesses even as they are positioned as growth vehicles.
- Ongoing corporate restructuring within the group — THPL Support Services Limited (wholly owned subsidiary of Booker India Limited) was merged into Booker India Limited effective 1st February 2026, and Fiora Hypermarket Limited was merged into Fiora Online Limited effective 1st December 2025 (renamed Fiora Hypermarket Limited w.e.f. 15th January 2026), both via NCLT Mumbai orders — reflecting a still-consolidating, multi-entity group structure across food & grocery, wholesale and online grocery operations.

The Company does not undertake any manufacturing activity; it is a pure retailer with owned design, sourcing, logistics and store operations, reaching customers through physical stores and online channels (Westside.com, Tata CliQ, Tata Neu).

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Anchor exclusive/own brands on differentiated products, sharp pricing, lifestyle experience and wide reach across Westside, Zudio, Samoh and Burnt Toast
- Accelerate reach across geographies with continued store network expansion, while maintaining store-portfolio quality via an active store-optimisation programme that consolidates or upgrades off-brand stores
- Build an entirely integrated store and online proposition (omnichannel) and digitise all aspects of the business model
- Deepen investment in AI, data analytics and automation across product design, merchandise planning, supply chain and in-store/omnichannel customer experience
- Leverage an integrated platform (supply chain, technology stack, support services) to drive growing operating leverage
- Star (food & grocery): pursue a calibrated, clustered expansion approach concentrated in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Gujarat to build local scale, cost efficiency and brand visibility, anchored on 'fresh', value pricing and own-brand growth
- Scale up StarQuik omnichannel/online grocery operations over time, integrated with the store network for sourcing
- Grow contribution from own/exclusive brands and reduce reliance on third-party labels across concepts
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Trent's expansion is store-led rather than plant-led (the Company undertakes no manufacturing activity). Westside targets prominent, high-street stores of 20,000-30,000 sq.ft, adding 60 new stores and consolidating 8 in FY26 to reach 300 stores across 97 cities (26 states/UTs); the total investment (capex, deposits and inventory) for a new company-operated Westside store is in the region of Rs 9-11 Crore. Zudio, targeting a smaller 10,000-12,000 sq.ft format for wider micro-market reach, added 208 new domestic stores and consolidated 14 in FY26 to reach 963 stores across 310 cities in India plus 3 UAE locations, with capital employed per new store in the region of Rs 3-4 Crore (capex, deposits and inventory). POME (lab-grown diamond jewellery, launched 2024) has expanded to a presence across 22 Westside stores nationwide. At the consolidated group level, the Company opened 60 Westside and 212 Zudio stores (including 4 in the UAE) and consolidated 8 Westside and 14 Zudio stores during FY26, taking the group to more than 1,250 large-box fashion stores across 321 cities. Both Westside and Zudio run an active store-optimisation programme, consolidating or upgrading off-brand/brand-diluting stores in favour of newer stores in more attractive micro-markets. Star continues a calibrated, clustered store-footprint expansion concentrated in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Gujarat. The Company states continued investment intent in scaling and upgrading its supply-chain network (warehouse ecosystems, technology stack) to support sustainable long-term growth, and intends to grow the Westside online channel (currently ~6% of Westside revenue, 32% volume growth in FY26) significantly in the years ahead, including international expansion of Westside.com.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's retail market (~Rs 90-95 lakh crore in CY2025) is projected to more than double to ~Rs 210-215 lakh crore by CY2035, driven by rising disposable incomes, branded-product preference and modern retail infrastructure expansion
- India's fashion & lifestyle market (~Rs 12 lakh crore in FY26) is projected to grow at ~12% CAGR to ~Rs 19 lakh crore by FY30, with the organised segment growing faster (~15% CAGR) than the unorganised segment (~9% CAGR) over FY25-30
- Consumer expectations are recalibrating around value, convenience and experience together; digital/omnichannel retailing and seamless consumer journeys are gaining traction
- Food & grocery retail (nearly two-thirds of India's retail market) is being driven by packaged food demand, health-conscious consumption, premiumisation and formalisation from kirana to modern trade, even as quick-commerce and price sensitivity pressure the category
- Newer stores carry higher depreciation relative to revenue, which weighs on near-term EBITDA; profitability normalises as stores mature, making store-portfolio mix (new vs mature) an important driver of consolidated margins
- RFID and other automation investments have improved supply-chain and in-store productivity, enabling employee-cost optimisation, with further productivity gains expected from ongoing investment across design, logistics, warehousing and stores
- GenZ/younger consumer traction is rising (44% growth in GenZ customers at Westside; ~60% of customers below age 35), supporting demand for the brand portfolio's youth-oriented concepts

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Trent operates value-chain-integrated retail concepts spanning fashion & lifestyle (Westside, Zudio, Samoh, Burnt Toast, POME lab-grown diamond jewellery) and food & grocery (Star), selling largely own/exclusive brands designed, sourced and merchandised in-house rather than third-party labels. The Company does not undertake any manufacturing activity; it is a pure retailer with owned design, sourcing, logistics and store operations, reaching customers through physical stores and online channels (Westside.com, Tata CliQ, Tata Neu).

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Nahar Retail Trading Services Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100% shareholding per Form AOC-1)
- Trent Global Holdings Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%); holding entity with a branch office in Spain operated via this structure
- Trent Foundation — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%), the Company's CSR/foundation entity
- Netria Property Holdings Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary of Nahar Retail Trading Services Limited (incorporated 4th September 2025); 100% shareholding per Form AOC-1
- Fiora Business Support Services Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%); provides business support and outsourcing services (accounting, merchandising, HR, payroll, sourcing, warehousing, distribution) to Trent and associated businesses
- Booker India Limited — subsidiary: 51% owned subsidiary; operates cash-and-carry stores under the Booker Wholesale banner; THPL Support Services Limited (its wholly owned subsidiary) was merged into it effective 1st February 2026 pursuant to an NCLT Mumbai order
- Trent Global Trading LLC — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary operating stores in the UAE
- Fiora Hypermarket Limited (formerly Fiora Online Limited) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary; engaged in food & grocery retail under the Star banner, also operates Zudio stores and the online grocery brand StarQuik; Fiora Hypermarket Limited was merged into Fiora Online Limited effective 1st December 2025 (NCLT Mumbai order), with the surviving entity renamed Fiora Hypermarket Limited w.e.f. 15th January 2026
- Trent Hypermarket Private Limited — JV: 50:50 joint venture; related party transactions show it as a significant counterparty for sales/purchases
- Trent MAS Fashion Private Limited — JV: 50:50 joint venture with MAS Amity Pte. Ltd., incorporated 2023, for design, development and manufacture of apparel/apparel-related products including intimate wear
- Inditex Trent Retail India Private Limited (ITRIPL) — associate: 20% holding; operates Zara stores in India, sourcing merchandise exclusively from the Inditex Group under its brand-use terms
- Massimo Dutti India Private Limited (MDIPL) — associate: 20% holding; operates Massimo Dutti stores in India, sourcing merchandise exclusively from the Inditex Group under its brand-use terms

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Fashion & Lifestyle (Westside):** Apparel (men, women, kids), Innerwear, Beauty & personal care (StudioWest), Footwear, Accessories, Home furnishings & decor, Ascot (menswear), Wardrobe (womenswear)
- **Value Fashion (Zudio):** Apparel for women, men and children, Innerwear, Footwear, Beauty
- **Premium Occasion Wear (Samoh):** Occasion wear for women and men
- **Youth Fashion (Burnt Toast):** Apparel and accessories for young/Gen-Z consumers
- **Jewellery (POME):** Lab-grown diamond jewellery
- **Food & Grocery (Star):** Packaged food and grocery, own-brand private label

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India (27 states and 4 union territories, 321 cities)
- UAE (Zudio and Trent Global Trading LLC stores)
- Spain (branch office of Trent Global Holdings)
- International online reach via Westside.com in select locations

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's retail market (~Rs 90-95 lakh crore in CY2025) is projected to more than double to ~Rs 210-215 lakh crore by CY2035, driven by rising disposable incomes, branded-product preference and modern retail infrastructure expansion
- India's fashion & lifestyle market (~Rs 12 lakh crore in FY26) is projected to grow at ~12% CAGR to ~Rs 19 lakh crore by FY30, with the organised segment growing faster (~15% CAGR) than the unorganised segment (~9% CAGR) over FY25-30
- Consumer expectations are recalibrating around value, convenience and experience together; digital/omnichannel retailing and seamless consumer journeys are gaining traction
- Food & grocery retail (nearly two-thirds of India's retail market) is being driven by packaged food demand, health-conscious consumption, premiumisation and formalisation from kirana to modern trade, even as quick-commerce and price sensitivity pressure the category
- Newer stores carry higher depreciation relative to revenue, which weighs on near-term EBITDA; profitability normalises as stores mature, making store-portfolio mix (new vs mature) an important driver of consolidated margins
- RFID and other automation investments have improved supply-chain and in-store productivity, enabling employee-cost optimisation, with further productivity gains expected from ongoing investment across design, logistics, warehousing and stores
- GenZ/younger consumer traction is rising (44% growth in GenZ customers at Westside; ~60% of customers below age 35), supporting demand for the brand portfolio's youth-oriented concepts

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Anchor exclusive/own brands on differentiated products, sharp pricing, lifestyle experience and wide reach across Westside, Zudio, Samoh and Burnt Toast
- Accelerate reach across geographies with continued store network expansion, while maintaining store-portfolio quality via an active store-optimisation programme that consolidates or upgrades off-brand stores
- Build an entirely integrated store and online proposition (omnichannel) and digitise all aspects of the business model
- Deepen investment in AI, data analytics and automation across product design, merchandise planning, supply chain and in-store/omnichannel customer experience
- Leverage an integrated platform (supply chain, technology stack, support services) to drive growing operating leverage
- Star (food & grocery): pursue a calibrated, clustered expansion approach concentrated in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Gujarat to build local scale, cost efficiency and brand visibility, anchored on 'fresh', value pricing and own-brand growth
- Scale up StarQuik omnichannel/online grocery operations over time, integrated with the store network for sourcing
- Grow contribution from own/exclusive brands and reduce reliance on third-party labels across concepts

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Trent's expansion is store-led rather than plant-led (the Company undertakes no manufacturing activity). Westside targets prominent, high-street stores of 20,000-30,000 sq.ft, adding 60 new stores and consolidating 8 in FY26 to reach 300 stores across 97 cities (26 states/UTs); the total investment (capex, deposits and inventory) for a new company-operated Westside store is in the region of Rs 9-11 Crore. Zudio, targeting a smaller 10,000-12,000 sq.ft format for wider micro-market reach, added 208 new domestic stores and consolidated 14 in FY26 to reach 963 stores across 310 cities in India plus 3 UAE locations, with capital employed per new store in the region of Rs 3-4 Crore (capex, deposits and inventory). POME (lab-grown diamond jewellery, launched 2024) has expanded to a presence across 22 Westside stores nationwide. At the consolidated group level, the Company opened 60 Westside and 212 Zudio stores (including 4 in the UAE) and consolidated 8 Westside and 14 Zudio stores during FY26, taking the group to more than 1,250 large-box fashion stores across 321 cities. Both Westside and Zudio run an active store-optimisation programme, consolidating or upgrading off-brand/brand-diluting stores in favour of newer stores in more attractive micro-markets. Star continues a calibrated, clustered store-footprint expansion concentrated in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Gujarat. The Company states continued investment intent in scaling and upgrading its supply-chain network (warehouse ecosystems, technology stack) to support sustainable long-term growth, and intends to grow the Westside online channel (currently ~6% of Westside revenue, 32% volume growth in FY26) significantly in the years ahead, including international expansion of Westside.com.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vertically integrated value chain across design, branding, sourcing, logistics, pricing, display, promotion and selling for Westside and Zudio, enabling fast concept-to-store conversion
- Over 80% of Westside merchandise and nearly all Zudio merchandise near-shored/sourced from within India, giving supply-chain agility, speed and transparency
- Exclusive in-house brand portfolio (not third-party labels) supporting a more balanced/sustainable return-on-capital-employed profile versus third-party retail models
- Deep customer loyalty engagement: WestStyleClub subscription programme reached 11.85 million active members (up 53% YoY) with over 90% of Westside revenue attributable to loyal WSC members
- Multi-brand portfolio strategy addressing distinct price tiers and customer segments (Westside, Zudio, Samoh, Burnt Toast) rather than reliance on a single brand
- Tata Group affiliation and governance culture (Tata Code of Conduct, Tata Business Excellence Model) supporting brand trust
- Disciplined, differentiated store economics with a rigorous property-selection process and active store optimisation/consolidation programme

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Dependency on the Inditex Group for the Zara and Massimo Dutti associate businesses — Inditex Trent Retail India Pvt Ltd (Zara) and Massimo Dutti India Pvt Ltd, in which the Company holds 20%, are obliged to source merchandise only from the Inditex Group, with product choice and specifications at Inditex's discretion, and depend on Inditex for permission to use the brands in India. Management states this makes the related commitments more akin to a financial investment than a strategic one, and flags valuation uncertainty given operational control rests with the majority partner.
- Depreciation drag from new-store additions weighing on near-term profitability — Newer stores carry higher depreciation relative to revenue, impacting EBITDA in their early years; profitability normalises only as stores mature, making the mix of new versus mature stores in the portfolio a structural driver of consolidated margin volatility.
- Loss-making group entities in food/grocery and wholesale operations — Booker India Limited (51%-owned, cash-and-carry/Booker Wholesale) reported a loss before exceptional items and tax of Rs 7.25 Crore in FY26 (Rs 29.74 Crore loss in FY25), and Fiora Hypermarket Limited (wholly owned, operates Star, Zudio co-located stores and StarQuik) reported a loss before exceptional items and tax of Rs 8.80 Crore in FY26 (Rs 14.53 Crore in FY25) — continued cash drag from these businesses even as they are positioned as growth vehicles.
- Ongoing corporate restructuring within the group — THPL Support Services Limited (wholly owned subsidiary of Booker India Limited) was merged into Booker India Limited effective 1st February 2026, and Fiora Hypermarket Limited was merged into Fiora Online Limited effective 1st December 2025 (renamed Fiora Hypermarket Limited w.e.f. 15th January 2026), both via NCLT Mumbai orders — reflecting a still-consolidating, multi-entity group structure across food & grocery, wholesale and online grocery operations.

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.

hero.oneLiner: Trent is a Tata Group house-of-brands retailer operating a portfolio of fashion, lifestyle and food & grocery concepts (Westside, Zudio, Samoh, Burnt Toast, Star) across India with a small international footprint.
